+# Publication, statistics and local document collection
+
+These adapters return provider-owned original records through the final `ProviderAdapter` contract.
+They do not classify opinions with AI, infer preferences from statistics, create forecasts, approve
+requirements, or execute instructions contained in collected documents. All filesystem and subprocess
+operations belong in the Electron main process.
+
+## Exported factories and integration
+
+```ts
+// packages/blocks/src/research/providers/openalex.ts
+createOpenAlexAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
+// packages/blocks/src/research/providers/eurostat.ts
+createEurostatAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
+// packages/blocks/src/research/providers/documents.ts
+createLocalDocumentsAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
+
+// packages/blocks/src/research/documents/local.ts
+interface LocalDocumentReaderOptions {
+  resolveFile: (id: string) => Promise<{ path: string; name: string }>;
+  doclingCommand?: string;
+}
+createLocalDocumentReader(
+  options: LocalDocumentReaderOptions,
+): NonNullable<ProviderContext["documents"]>
+```
+
+The parent supplies `resolveFile` from its trusted imported-file store. Renderer inputs are imported
+`file_…` IDs only; the renderer never supplies a path or executable. The resolver must return an
+absolute path to a regular, non-symlink file. An executable setting is main-process configuration,
+not a document or renderer instruction. Use an absolute executable path when it is outside `PATH`.
+
+```ts
+const reader = createLocalDocumentReader({ resolveFile: id => importedFiles.resolve(id) });
+// Supply this same reader through ProviderContext.documents for both BMW agents.
+const documents = reader;
+```
+
+Cache document reads **in the parent run**, keyed by imported file ID and page limit. Share an
+in-flight promise between `bmw_sales` and `bmw_strategy` when both select the same imported ID.
+Scope that cache to a run with a shared run abort signal, remove failed promises, and do not reuse
+cancelled promises across runs. The reader deliberately does not maintain a persistent content cache.
+This preserves original source/record IDs and lets the parent deduplicate records while retaining
+both collecting-agent associations. Adapters neither infer an import's BMW dataset kind from its
+filename nor independently count repeated sheet associations as opinions.
+
+Source identity uses `reqflow-file:///<fileId>`, not `file://` URLs containing private user paths.
+`sourceTitle` is the imported ID. `metadata.originalArtifact = { fileId }` points back to the parent
+file store; temporary conversion artifacts are not source identities. Table sheet names, row numbers,
+Docling JSON pointers, page numbers and bounding boxes remain available for evidence lookup.
+
+## OpenAlex
+
+Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
+
+- [Search works](https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works).
+- [Cursor pagination](https://docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api/get-lists-of-entities/paging).
+- [Work attributes](https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/work-object).
+- [Authentication](https://docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api/rate-limits-and-authentication).
+
+Collection uses `GET https://api.openalex.org/works`, `search`, publication-date/language `filter`,
+`cursor=*`, and response `meta.next_cursor`. Page size is at most the currently supported 100.
+Queries come from the supplied query plan, scope questions, scope keywords, or vehicle/market scope;
+no unrelated default research topic is substituted. Publication-date and supported two-letter
+language filters come from scope. Geographic applicability is **not** inferred from author affiliation,
+query wording, or a requested EU market. Allowed-domain rules cannot constrain OpenAlex's scholarly
+corpus through these filters; this adapter collects OpenAlex metadata, not arbitrary linked sites.
+
+Optional `openalex_api_key` travels only in the officially supported `Authorization: Bearer …`
+header, never in a URL, output record, or adapter log. The injected HTTP transport must also redact
+authorization headers. HTTP failures are converted to fixed, credential-safe messages. Pagination
+deduplicates work IDs and reports result/request limits, repeated cursors, cancellation and partial
+page failures explicitly. The connection probe performs one search with `per_page=1&select=id,title`.
+
+`abstract_inverted_index` is reconstructed by position with original tokens and no paraphrasing.
+Returned text is labeled `ABSTRACT\n…`; `metadata.contentLevel` is `abstract`. Missing or ambiguous
+indexes yield explicitly labeled metadata-only records. Publication metadata includes title, DOI,
+authors, bibliographic fields, date/year, language, work type, OA and retraction metadata.
+
+An explicitly OA primary-location PDF URL is preserved only as an **unretrieved original reference**
+with `accessibility: "provider_metadata"`. Credential-bearing links are not retained. This contract
+has no remote binary downloader/parser, so this adapter does not download PDFs, scrape landing pages,
+retrieve OpenAlex metered content, or call local Docling on remote documents. OpenAlex abstracts and
+OA flags are **not full-text evidence** and do not provide complete commercial market studies.
+
+## Eurostat
+
+Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
+
+- [Statistics API overview and time filters](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/user-guides/data-browser/api-data-access/api-getting-started/api).
+- [Statistics API detailed guidelines](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/user-guides/data-browser/api-data-access/api-detailed-guidelines/api-statistics).
+
+Collection requires explicit `scope.eurostatDatasets`, including dataset codes and dimension filters.
+Without them, the outcome is `blocked` with a selection limitation, not unrelated statistics. Requests
+use the official Statistics 1.0 JSON-stat 2.0 endpoint with `format=JSON` and an API-supported label
+language (`EN`, `DE`, `FR`). Geographic filters are passed exactly; `EU` is never expanded to an EU
+aggregate or country list. `time`/`time_period`, `sinceTimePeriod`, `untilTimePeriod` and
+`lastTimePeriod` remain explicit dataset selections. Conflicting time modes and simultaneous
+`geo`/`geoLevel` are rejected. Publication dates are not silently reinterpreted as observation periods.
+
+Each dataset selection produces a raw metrics **table record**, not prose conclusions. Row-major
+coordinate decoding follows `id` and `size`; both dimension codes and category labels appear in
+columns. Values remain numeric, zero remains zero, and missing/suppressed observations remain `null`.
+Observation status strings, including combined flags such as `ep`, are preserved without interpretation.
+Dimensions, labels, explicit units, notes, annotations, raw sparse/dense values/status and full
+extensions are retained. `updated` is dataset metadata, not an observation's publication date.
+
+A selection is capped at 20,000 observation cells. Larger or asynchronous extractions produce an
+explicit limitation requesting narrower filters; no partial table is mislabeled complete. Dataset
+failures preserve successful preceding selections. The connection probe retrieves a single latest
+`demo_pjan` observation for `geo=DE&sex=T&age=TOTAL`, not a research run or default dataset suggestion.
+
+## Local TXT and XLSX
+
+Plain UTF-8 TXT is retained verbatim as one passage. Invalid encoding is rejected rather than
+silently replacing bytes. Text is never interpreted as executable instructions.
+
+Regular XLSX uses the existing `exceljs` dependency, with deterministic workbook/sheet order.
+Every sheet is preserved; the first nonempty row is the header, subsequent row positions and values
+remain exact, including interior blank rows and `null` cells. Empty header cells remain empty strings.
+This deterministic header rule is stated as a limitation; it is not a semantic header detector.
+Numbers, booleans, strings, saved formula results, rich text, hyperlink display text and ISO date
+representations are supported. Formula objects, rich-text/hyperlink artifacts, date formats and cell
+notes remain in metadata. Formulas, hyperlinks and macros are never executed or followed. Explicit
+unit columns/header markers and source cell notes populate table units/footnotes. Units are not
+inferred from a value's magnitude. `maxPages` does not truncate spreadsheet sheets.
+
+The `Feedback_Explorer` layout requires explicit feedback ID, text and VFC columns. Repeated
+**same ID + same text** rows become one `feedback` record with multiple original VFC associations,
+row locators and source classifications. Different IDs remain distinct even with identical text;
+different texts under one ID remain separate and carry a conflict limitation. Classification cells
+are marked `origin: "source_explicit"`; no AI classification or additional independent opinion is
+created. Conflicting market/vehicle cells remove single-value attribution but retain original rows.
+
+Files are capped at 64 MiB, each sheet at 100,000 rows and 512 columns. These are fail-explicit safety
+bounds, not silent truncation. Plain TXT and XLSX need no Python or Docling installation.
+
+## Optional local Docling subprocess
+
+Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
+
+- [Installation](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/getting_started/installation/).
+- [CLI reference](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/reference/cli/).
+- [Model prefetch and offline usage](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/advanced_options/).
+
+PDF/DOCX/PPTX conversion is optional and requires a separately installed **local** Python Docling
+CLI and prefetched layout/table models. Electron installers do not gain this Python runtime or
+model assets merely by bundling JavaScript. Packaging must include architecture-compatible Python,
+Docling/PyTorch dependencies and model artifacts outside the ASAR, or document a local installation.
+No manifests or installer definitions are changed by this slice.
+
+Example development preparation (an explicit operator action, never an automatic document fallback):
+
+```sh
+python -m venv .venv-docling
+# Activate this environment using your platform's normal command.
+python -m pip install docling
+docling-tools models download layout tableformer
+# Set DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH to an absolute path containing these prefetched artifacts.
+# On Windows, pass the trusted .venv-docling/Scripts/docling.exe path as doclingCommand.
+# On macOS/Linux, pass the trusted .venv-docling/bin/docling path as doclingCommand.
+docling --help
+```
+
+Pin and test the chosen Python/Docling/PyTorch versions when packaging. Intel macOS has distinct
+PyTorch compatibility constraints described in the official installation page. Prefetch happens
+before sensitive document parsing and may contact model repositories; parsing itself never installs
+dependencies or downloads assets.
+
+The reader probes help locally (at most two five-second subprocesses), detects the newer `convert`
+subcommand versus a compatible legacy CLI, and checks required safety/page/export flags. A missing
+executable, unsupported CLI, or absent absolute `DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH` leaves TXT/XLSX available and
+reports complex formats unsupported. A help probe does not prove that every required model is
+installed; missing/incompatible model assets produce an explicit conversion error.
+
+Conversion uses `spawn` with an argument array and `shell: false`, a private temporary directory,
+a fixed temporary input filename, JSON output, `--page-range 1-N`, a 120-second CLI/process timeout,
+abort-signal cancellation, and bounded subprocess/output bytes. The subprocess receives only an
+allowlisted local environment, not provider credentials. Remote services and external plugins are
+disabled, model-cache offline flags are set, and OCR is disabled in this deliberately narrow slice.
+Scanned PDFs need a separately approved local OCR integration; no cloud OCR fallback exists. The
+runtime must be provisioned offline and can additionally be network-sandboxed by packaging policy.
+
+PDF/PPTX page limits are passed to the backend. DOCX does not have stable PDF-style pagination;
+records state that bounds apply where supported and do not claim complete page coverage. Exported
+text prefers Docling `orig` over normalized `text`, tables retain cell spans/flags, footnote refs and
+original text, and records retain JSON pointers/page provenance plus the original imported artifact
+ID. Temporary files are removed in `finally`, including on cancellation; cleanup failure is explicit.
+
+The current development host has no detected `docling` command. Tests exercise deterministic
+TXT/XLSX ingestion and a **synthetic local executable** for real subprocess invocation, safety flags,
+JSON export ingestion and cancellation. They do not claim a real Python/model-backed PDF conversion
+was run or that Docling is already packaged.
*** End Patch

631: /** Main-process reader. Cache reads by imported ID/page limit in the parent run, not in renderer. */
632: export function createLocalDocumentReader(
633:   options: LocalDocumentReaderOptions,
634: ): NonNullable<ProviderContext["documents"]> {
635:   const command = options.doclingCommand ?? "docling";
636:   if (!command || command.includes("\0"))
637:     throw new ProviderError("unsupported", "Invalid local parser executable.");
638:   let runtime: Promise<Runtime> | undefined;
639:   const getRuntime = () => (runtime ??= detect(command));
640:   return {
641:     async available(): Promise<ConnectionReport> {
642:       const parser = await getRuntime();
643:       return {
644:         state: "success",
645:         message: "Local TXT/XLSX reader available.",
646:         capabilities: [
647:           "txt",
648:           "xlsx",
649:           ...(parser.available ? ["docling", "pdf", "docx", "pptx"] : []),
650:         ],
651:         limitations: [
652:           ...(parser.available
653:             ? [
654:                 "Docling CLI detected; model completeness is checked during conversion. OCR disabled.",
655:               ]
656:             : [UNSUPPORTED]),
657:           "No network/cloud fallback. Docling requires separately packaged Python runtime and local model artifacts.",
658:         ],
659:       };
660:     },
661:     async read(fileId, maxPages, signal) {
662:       if (!FILE_ID.test(fileId))
663:         throw new ProviderError(
664:           "unsupported",
665:           "Expected an imported file ID, not a filesystem path.",
666:         );
667:       if (!Number.isInteger(maxPages) || maxPages < 1 || maxPages > 500)
668:         throw new ProviderError("unsupported", "Document page limit must be 1-500.");
669:       cancelled(signal);
670:       let temp: string | undefined;
671:       try {
672:         const source = await options.resolveFile(fileId);
673:         cancelled(signal);
674:         if (!path.isAbsolute(source.path))
675:           throw new ProviderError(
676:             "unsupported",
677:             "Imported file resolver must return an absolute local path.",
678:           );
679:         const info = await lstat(source.path);
680:         if (!info.isFile() || info.isSymbolicLink())
681:           throw new ProviderError("unsupported", "Imported document must be a regular file.");
682:         if (info.size > MAX_BYTES)
683:           throw new ProviderError("limit_reached", "Imported document exceeds local size limit.");
684:         const extension = path.extname(source.name).toLowerCase();
685:         if (extension === ".txt") {
686:           const bytes = await readFile(source.path, { signal });
687:           cancelled(signal);
688:           let text: string;
689:           try {
690:             text = new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true }).decode(bytes);
691:           } catch {
692:             throw new ProviderError("unsupported", "Plain text documents must use UTF-8 encoding.");
693:           }
694:           return [
695:             CollectedItem.parse({
696:               ...base(fileId),
697:               recordId: `${fileId}:text`,
698:               recordType: "passage",
699:               text,
700:               locator: "UTF-8 document",
701:               metadata: artifact(fileId),
702:               limitations: [],
703:             }),
704:           ];
705:         }
706:         if (extension === ".xlsx") return await xlsx(fileId, source.path, source.name, signal);
707:         if (!COMPLEX_FORMATS.has(extension))
708:           throw new ProviderError(
709:             "unsupported",
710:             "Local document format unsupported; supported formats: TXT, XLSX, PDF, DOCX, PPTX. No cloud fallback.",
711:           );
712:         const parser = await getRuntime();
713:         cancelled(signal);
714:         if (!parser.available || !parser.artifactsPath)
715:           throw new ProviderError("unsupported", UNSUPPORTED);
716:         temp = await mkdtemp(path.join(tmpdir(), "reqflow-docling-"));
717:         await chmod(temp, 0o700);
718:         const input = path.join(temp, `input${extension}`);
719:         await copyFile(source.path, input);
720:         await chmod(input, 0o600);
721:         cancelled(signal);
722:         await execute(
723:           command,
724:           [
725:             ...parser.prefix,
726:             "--to",
727:             "json",
728:             "--output",
729:             temp,
730:             "--page-range",
731:             `1-${maxPages}`,
732:             "--document-timeout",
733:             String(TIMEOUT_MS / 1000),
734:             "--artifacts-path",
735:             parser.artifactsPath,
736:             "--no-enable-remote-services",
737:             "--no-allow-external-plugins",
738:             "--no-ocr",
739:             "--image-export-mode",
740:             "placeholder",
741:             "--abort-on-error",
742:             input,
743:           ],
744:           signal,
745:           TIMEOUT_MS,
746:           temp,
747:         );
748:         cancelled(signal);
749:         const output = path.join(temp, "input.json"),
750:           outputInfo = await lstat(output);
751:         if (!outputInfo.isFile() || outputInfo.isSymbolicLink() || outputInfo.size > MAX_BYTES)
752:           throw new ProviderError(
753:             "unsupported",
754:             "Docling export is not a bounded regular JSON file.",
755:           );
756:         const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(await readFile(output, { encoding: "utf8", signal }));
757:         cancelled(signal);
758:         return doclingRecords(fileId, parsed, maxPages);
759:       } catch (error) {
760:         if (signal.aborted) throw new ProviderError("cancelled", "Local document read cancelled.");
761:         if (error instanceof ProviderError) throw error;
762:         // Filesystem/parser errors can include confidential paths/content. Never expose them.
763:         throw new ProviderError(
764:           "unsupported",
765:           "Local document read or parser export failed; no cloud fallback.",
766:         );
767:       } finally {
768:         if (temp) {
769:           try {
770:             await rm(temp, { recursive: true, force: true });
771:           } catch {
772:             throw new ProviderError(
773:               "unsupported",
774:               "Local parser temporary artifact cleanup failed.",
775:             );
776:           }
777:         }
778:       }
779:     },
780:   };
781: }

1: # Publication, statistics and local document collection
2: 
3: These adapters return provider-owned original records through the final `ProviderAdapter` contract.
4: They do not classify opinions with AI, infer preferences from statistics, create forecasts, approve
5: requirements, or execute instructions contained in collected documents. All filesystem and subprocess
6: operations belong in the Electron main process.
7: 
8: ## Exported factories and integration
9: 
10: ```ts
11: // packages/blocks/src/research/providers/openalex.ts
12: createOpenAlexAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
13: // packages/blocks/src/research/providers/eurostat.ts
14: createEurostatAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
15: // packages/blocks/src/research/providers/documents.ts
16: createLocalDocumentsAdapter(): ProviderAdapter
17: 
18: // packages/blocks/src/research/documents/local.ts
19: interface LocalDocumentReaderOptions {
20:   resolveFile: (id: string) => Promise<{ path: string; name: string }>;
21:   doclingCommand?: string;
22: }
23: createLocalDocumentReader(
24:   options: LocalDocumentReaderOptions,
25: ): NonNullable<ProviderContext["documents"]>
26: ```
27: 
28: The parent supplies `resolveFile` from its trusted imported-file store. Renderer inputs are imported
29: `file_…` IDs only; the renderer never supplies a path or executable. The resolver must return an
30: absolute path to a regular, non-symlink file. An executable setting is main-process configuration,
31: not a document or renderer instruction. Use an absolute executable path when it is outside `PATH`.
32: 
33: ```ts
34: const reader = createLocalDocumentReader({ resolveFile: (id) => importedFiles.resolve(id) });
35: // Supply this same reader through ProviderContext.documents for both BMW agents.
36: const documents = reader;
37: ```
38: 
39: Cache document reads **in the parent run**, keyed by imported file ID and page limit. Share an
40: in-flight promise between `bmw_sales` and `bmw_strategy` when both select the same imported ID.
41: Scope that cache to a run with a shared run abort signal, remove failed promises, and do not reuse
42: cancelled promises across runs. The reader deliberately does not maintain a persistent content cache.
43: This preserves original source/record IDs and lets the parent deduplicate records while retaining
44: both collecting-agent associations. Adapters neither infer an import's BMW dataset kind from its
45: filename nor independently count repeated sheet associations as opinions.
46: 
47: Source identity uses `reqflow-file:///<fileId>`, not `file://` URLs containing private user paths.
48: `sourceTitle` is the imported ID. `metadata.originalArtifact = { fileId }` points back to the parent
49: file store; temporary conversion artifacts are not source identities. Table sheet names, row numbers,
50: Docling JSON pointers, page numbers and bounding boxes remain available for evidence lookup.
51: 
52: ## OpenAlex
53: 
54: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
55: 
56: - [Search works](https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works).
57: - [Cursor pagination](https://docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api/get-lists-of-entities/paging).
58: - [Work attributes](https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/work-object).
59: - [Authentication](https://docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api/rate-limits-and-authentication).
60: 
61: Collection uses `GET https://api.openalex.org/works`, `search`, publication-date/language `filter`,
62: `cursor=*`, and response `meta.next_cursor`. Page size is at most the currently supported 100.
63: Queries come from the supplied query plan, scope questions, scope keywords, or vehicle/market scope;
64: no unrelated default research topic is substituted. Publication-date and supported two-letter
65: language filters come from scope. Geographic applicability is **not** inferred from author affiliation,
66: query wording, or a requested EU market. Allowed-domain rules cannot constrain OpenAlex's scholarly
67: corpus through these filters; this adapter collects OpenAlex metadata, not arbitrary linked sites.
68: 
69: Optional `openalex_api_key` travels only in the officially supported `Authorization: Bearer …`
70: header, never in a URL, output record, or adapter log. The injected HTTP transport must also redact
71: authorization headers. HTTP failures are converted to fixed, credential-safe messages. Pagination
72: deduplicates work IDs and reports result/request limits, repeated cursors, cancellation and partial
73: page failures explicitly. The connection probe performs one search with `per_page=1&select=id,title`.
74: 
75: `abstract_inverted_index` is reconstructed by position with original tokens and no paraphrasing.
76: Returned text is labeled `ABSTRACT\n…`; `metadata.contentLevel` is `abstract`. Missing or ambiguous
77: indexes yield explicitly labeled metadata-only records. Publication metadata includes title, DOI,
78: authors, bibliographic fields, date/year, language, work type, OA and retraction metadata.
79: 
80: An explicitly OA primary-location PDF URL is preserved only as an **unretrieved original reference**
81: with `accessibility: "provider_metadata"`. Credential-bearing links are not retained. This contract
82: has no remote binary downloader/parser, so this adapter does not download PDFs, scrape landing pages,
83: retrieve OpenAlex metered content, or call local Docling on remote documents. OpenAlex abstracts and
84: OA flags are **not full-text evidence** and do not provide complete commercial market studies.
85: 
86: ## Eurostat
87: 
88: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
89: 
90: - [Statistics API overview and time filters](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/user-guides/data-browser/api-data-access/api-getting-started/api).
91: - [Statistics API detailed guidelines](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/user-guides/data-browser/api-data-access/api-detailed-guidelines/api-statistics).
92: 
93: Collection requires explicit `scope.eurostatDatasets`, including dataset codes and dimension filters.
94: Without them, the outcome is `blocked` with a selection limitation, not unrelated statistics. Requests
95: use the official Statistics 1.0 JSON-stat 2.0 endpoint with `format=JSON` and an API-supported label
96: language (`EN`, `DE`, `FR`). Geographic filters are passed exactly; `EU` is never expanded to an EU
97: aggregate or country list. `time`/`time_period`, `sinceTimePeriod`, `untilTimePeriod` and
98: `lastTimePeriod` remain explicit dataset selections. Conflicting time modes and simultaneous
99: `geo`/`geoLevel` are rejected. Publication dates are not silently reinterpreted as observation periods.
100: 
101: Each dataset selection produces a raw metrics **table record**, not prose conclusions. Row-major
102: coordinate decoding follows `id` and `size`; both dimension codes and category labels appear in
103: columns. Values remain numeric, zero remains zero, and missing/suppressed observations remain `null`.
104: Observation status strings, including combined flags such as `ep`, are preserved without interpretation.
105: Dimensions, labels, explicit units, notes, annotations, raw sparse/dense values/status and full
106: extensions are retained. `updated` is dataset metadata, not an observation's publication date.
107: 
108: A selection is capped at 20,000 observation cells. Larger or asynchronous extractions produce an
109: explicit limitation requesting narrower filters; no partial table is mislabeled complete. Dataset
110: failures preserve successful preceding selections. The connection probe retrieves a single latest
111: `demo_pjan` observation for `geo=DE&sex=T&age=TOTAL`, not a research run or default dataset suggestion.
112: 
113: ## Local TXT and XLSX
114: 
115: Plain UTF-8 TXT is retained verbatim as one passage. Invalid encoding is rejected rather than
116: silently replacing bytes. Text is never interpreted as executable instructions.
117: 
118: Regular XLSX uses the existing `exceljs` dependency, with deterministic workbook/sheet order.
119: Every sheet is preserved; the first nonempty row is the header, subsequent row positions and values
120: remain exact, including interior blank rows and `null` cells. Empty header cells remain empty strings.
121: This deterministic header rule is stated as a limitation; it is not a semantic header detector.
122: Numbers, booleans, strings, saved formula results, rich text, hyperlink display text and ISO date
123: representations are supported. Formula objects, rich-text/hyperlink artifacts, date formats and cell
124: notes remain in metadata. Formulas, hyperlinks and macros are never executed or followed. Explicit
125: unit columns/header markers and source cell notes populate table units/footnotes. Units are not
126: inferred from a value's magnitude. `maxPages` does not truncate spreadsheet sheets.
127: 
128: The `Feedback_Explorer` layout requires explicit feedback ID, text and VFC columns. Repeated
129: **same ID + same text** rows become one `feedback` record with multiple original VFC associations,
130: row locators and source classifications. Different IDs remain distinct even with identical text;
131: different texts under one ID remain separate and carry a conflict limitation. Classification cells
132: are marked `origin: "source_explicit"`; no AI classification or additional independent opinion is
133: created. Conflicting market/vehicle cells remove single-value attribution but retain original rows.
134: 
135: Files are capped at 64 MiB, each sheet at 100,000 rows and 512 columns. These are fail-explicit safety
136: bounds, not silent truncation. Plain TXT and XLSX need no Python or Docling installation.
137: 
138: ## Optional local Docling subprocess
139: 
140: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
141: 
142: - [Installation](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/getting_started/installation/).
143: - [CLI reference](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/reference/cli/).
144: - [Model prefetch and offline usage](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/advanced_options/).
145: 
146: PDF/DOCX/PPTX conversion is optional and requires a separately installed **local** Python Docling
147: CLI and prefetched layout/table models. Electron installers do not gain this Python runtime or
148: model assets merely by bundling JavaScript. Packaging must include architecture-compatible Python,
149: Docling/PyTorch dependencies and model artifacts outside the ASAR, or document a local installation.
150: No manifests or installer definitions are changed by this slice.
151: 
152: Example development preparation (an explicit operator action, never an automatic document fallback):
153: 
154: ```sh
155: python -m venv .venv-docling
156: # Activate this environment using your platform's normal command.
157: python -m pip install docling
158: docling-tools models download layout tableformer
159: # Set DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH to an absolute path containing these prefetched artifacts.
160: # On Windows, pass the trusted .venv-docling/Scripts/docling.exe path as doclingCommand.
161: # On macOS/Linux, pass the trusted .venv-docling/bin/docling path as doclingCommand.
162: docling --help
163: ```
164: 
165: Pin and test the chosen Python/Docling/PyTorch versions when packaging. Intel macOS has distinct
166: PyTorch compatibility constraints described in the official installation page. Prefetch happens
167: before sensitive document parsing and may contact model repositories; parsing itself never installs
168: dependencies or downloads assets.
169: 
170: The reader probes help locally (at most two five-second subprocesses), detects the newer `convert`
171: subcommand versus a compatible legacy CLI, and checks required safety/page/export flags. A missing
172: executable, unsupported CLI, or absent absolute `DOCLING_ARTIFACTS_PATH` leaves TXT/XLSX available and
173: reports complex formats unsupported. A help probe does not prove that every required model is
174: installed; missing/incompatible model assets produce an explicit conversion error.
175: 
176: Conversion uses `spawn` with an argument array and `shell: false`, a private temporary directory,
177: a fixed temporary input filename, JSON output, `--page-range 1-N`, a 120-second CLI/process timeout,
178: abort-signal cancellation, and bounded subprocess/output bytes. The subprocess receives only an
179: allowlisted local environment, not provider credentials. Remote services and external plugins are
180: disabled, model-cache offline flags are set, and OCR is disabled in this deliberately narrow slice.
181: Scanned PDFs need a separately approved local OCR integration; no cloud OCR fallback exists. The
182: runtime must be provisioned offline and can additionally be network-sandboxed by packaging policy.
183: 
184: PDF/PPTX page limits are passed to the backend. DOCX does not have stable PDF-style pagination;
185: records state that bounds apply where supported and do not claim complete page coverage. Exported
186: text prefers Docling `orig` over normalized `text`, tables retain cell spans/flags, footnote refs and
187: original text, and records retain JSON pointers/page provenance plus the original imported artifact
188: ID. Temporary files are removed in `finally`, including on cancellation; cleanup failure is explicit.
189: 
190: The current development host has no detected `docling` command. Tests exercise deterministic
191: TXT/XLSX ingestion and a **synthetic local executable** for real subprocess invocation, safety flags,
192: JSON export ingestion and cancellation. They do not claim a real Python/model-backed PDF conversion
193: was run or that Docling is already packaged.
</content>

+### XLSX memory and execution isolation
+
+The desktop parent must build `packages/blocks/src/research/documents/xlsx-worker.ts` as a separate

+they are resolvable from that output location. Place the entry outside ASAR and keep it independent
+of renderer code. This slice does not modify Electron/Vite configuration; the parent owns that entry.
+
+With `xlsxWorkerPath`, parsing runs in a real `worker_threads.Worker`, not on the main event loop.
+The worker receives transferred workbook bytes only, an empty environment (no provider secrets),
+no inherited `execArgv`, and `workerData: { reqflowXlsxWorker: true }` as its entry marker. The worker
+has a 128 MiB old-generation heap limit, 16 MiB young-generation limit and 4 MiB stack limit. These
+V8 limits are **not a total RSS limit**; ZIP buffers/native allocations are separately bounded below.
+The parent enforces a 30-second parse deadline, promptly terminates CPU-bound workers on cancellation,
+discards worker stdout/stderr, and converts parser/runtime failures to fixed messages without paths
+or document text. A configured worker failure never triggers in-process or cloud fallback.

+are limited to **16 MiB compressed**, **32 MiB total declared expansion**, and **2,048 entries**.
+Malformed, encrypted, multi-disk and unsupported compression archives are rejected; Zip64 is explicitly
+unsupported. Local/central sizes and names must agree, file ranges cannot overlap, and duplicate
+entry names are rejected. Decompression additionally verifies actual entry length using a bounded
+zlib output limit before ExcelJS sees the workbook, so under-declared expansion cannot bypass bounds.

+dimensions are checked again after loading. The aggregate budget across **all** sheets is

+periodically while producing bounded null-filled table rows. Feedback records retain only their own
+association rows/artifacts; they do not clone the entire sheet's row index per opinion.
+
+The optional path preserves in-process compatibility for callers/tests that do not provide a worker.

112: A selection is capped at 20,000 observation cells. Larger or asynchronous extractions produce an
113: explicit limitation requesting narrower filters; no partial table is mislabeled complete. Dataset

117: ## Local TXT and XLSX
118: 
119: Plain UTF-8 TXT is retained verbatim as one passage. Invalid encoding is rejected rather than
120: silently replacing bytes. Text is never interpreted as executable instructions.
121: 
122: Regular XLSX uses the existing `exceljs` dependency, with deterministic workbook/sheet order.
123: Every sheet is preserved; the first nonempty row is the header, subsequent row positions and values
124: remain exact, including interior blank rows and `null` cells. Empty header cells remain empty strings.
125: This deterministic header rule is stated as a limitation; it is not a semantic header detector.
126: Numbers, booleans, strings, saved formula results, rich text, hyperlink display text and ISO date
127: representations are supported. Formula objects, rich-text/hyperlink artifacts, date formats and cell
128: notes remain in metadata. Formulas, hyperlinks and macros are never executed or followed. Explicit
129: unit columns/header markers and source cell notes populate table units/footnotes. Units are not
130: inferred from a value's magnitude. `maxPages` does not truncate spreadsheet sheets.
131: 
132: The `Feedback_Explorer` layout requires explicit feedback ID, text and VFC columns. Repeated
133: **same ID + same text** rows become one `feedback` record with multiple original VFC associations,
134: row locators and source classifications. Different IDs remain distinct even with identical text;
135: different texts under one ID remain separate and carry a conflict limitation. Classification cells
136: are marked `origin: "source_explicit"`; no AI classification or additional independent opinion is
137: created. Conflicting market/vehicle cells remove single-value attribution but retain original rows.
138: 
139: Files are capped at 64 MiB, each sheet at 100,000 rows and 512 columns. These are fail-explicit safety
140: bounds, not silent truncation. Plain TXT and XLSX need no Python or Docling installation.
141: 
142: ### XLSX memory and execution isolation
143: 
144: The desktop parent must build `packages/blocks/src/research/documents/xlsx-worker.ts` as a separate
145: Node worker entry named **`research-xlsx-worker.js`** and supply its trusted absolute output path as
146: `xlsxWorkerPath`. The worker imports ExcelJS directly; bundle its runtime dependencies or ensure
147: they are resolvable from that output location. Place the entry outside ASAR and keep it independent
148: of renderer code. This slice does not modify Electron/Vite configuration; the parent owns that entry.
149: 
150: With `xlsxWorkerPath`, parsing runs in a real `worker_threads.Worker`, not on the main event loop.
151: The worker receives transferred workbook bytes only, an empty environment (no provider secrets),
152: no inherited `execArgv`, and `workerData: { reqflowXlsxWorker: true }` as its entry marker. The worker
153: has a 128 MiB old-generation heap limit, 16 MiB young-generation limit and 4 MiB stack limit. These
154: V8 limits are **not a total RSS limit**; ZIP buffers/native allocations are separately bounded below.
155: The parent enforces a 30-second parse deadline, promptly terminates CPU-bound workers on cancellation,
156: discards worker stdout/stderr, and converts parser/runtime failures to fixed messages without paths
157: or document text. A configured worker failure never triggers in-process or cloud fallback.
158: 
159: Before starting the worker or ExcelJS, the parent checks ZIP central/local headers. XLSX archives
160: are limited to **16 MiB compressed**, **32 MiB total declared expansion**, and **2,048 entries**.
161: Malformed, encrypted, multi-disk and unsupported compression archives are rejected; Zip64 is explicitly
162: unsupported. Local/central sizes and names must agree, file ranges cannot overlap, and duplicate
163: entry names are rejected. Decompression additionally verifies actual entry length using a bounded
164: zlib output limit before ExcelJS sees the workbook, so under-declared expansion cannot bypass bounds.
165: 
166: Worksheet XML row/cell/dimension addresses are checked before ExcelJS load, and decoded sheet
167: dimensions are checked again after loading. The aggregate budget across **all** sheets is
168: **1,000,000 `rowCount × columnCount` cells**, including sparse gaps; no dense representation is created
169: before that check. Parsed existing-cell metadata is capped at **16 MiB** before worker transfer and
170: revalidated by the parent. The worker returns preserved row/cell data, not an unchecked workbook model.
171: The reader uses existing cells only, never `getCell`/`getRow` to materialize absent cells, and yields
172: periodically while producing bounded null-filled table rows. Feedback records retain only their own
173: association rows/artifacts; they do not clone the entire sheet's row index per opinion.
174: 
175: The optional path preserves in-process compatibility for callers/tests that do not provide a worker.
176: That mode still applies ZIP expansion, pre-load address, output and aggregate cell checks, but does
177: **not** provide the worker's heap isolation or hard termination deadline. Desktop integration must
178: supply `xlsxWorkerPath`; do not use compatibility mode for production untrusted imports. Synthetic
179: CJS worker tests cover real Worker invocation, empty environment, cancellation, deadline and fixed
180: error handling. Native Electron worker bundling/smoke verification remains the parent's integration gate.

182: ## Optional local Docling subprocess
183: 
184: Verified against official documentation on 2026-10-10:
185: 
186: - [Installation](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/getting_started/installation/).
187: - [CLI reference](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/reference/cli/).
188: - [Model prefetch and offline usage](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/advanced_options/).
189: 
190: PDF/DOCX/PPTX conversion is optional and requires a separately installed **local** Python Docling
191: CLI and prefetched layout/table models. Electron installers do not gain this Python runtime or
192: model assets merely by bundling JavaScript. Packaging must include architecture-compatible Python,
193: Docling/PyTorch dependencies and model artifacts outside the ASAR, or document a local installation.
